assumptions.condition: The integers \(J,K,L,r\) are fixed, \(L\ge r\), and \(1\le r\le\min\{L,J\}\).
The known blocks are contiguous, \(n_\ell/n\to p_\ell\in[c_{\mathrm{lo}},1]\) for every \(\ell\), and \(T_1/n\to\lambda\in[c_{\mathrm{lo}},C_{\mathrm{hi}}]\).

For a pre-treatment date in block \(\ell\), the untreated mean vector is \((a_{0\ell},A_{\ell\cdot})=(f_\ell^{\prime}\mu_0,f_\ell^{\prime}U_D)\); in the stable post regime, the untreated target and donor means are \((f_{\mathrm{post}}^{\prime}\mu_0,d^{\prime})\).

standard.name: fixed-rank linear factor model with regime-constant means

assumptions.condition: The entries of \(F_{\mathrm{pre}},U_D,\mu_0,f_{\mathrm{post}}\) and the operator norm of \(S\) are bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{hi}}\).
The matrix \(A\) has rank \(r\), and each of its \(r\) nonzero singular values belongs to \([c_{\mathrm{lo}},C_{\mathrm{hi}}]\).
The process \((\varepsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) is strictly stationary and satisfies \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t]=0\).
The vector sub-Gaussian norm satisfies \(\lVert\varepsilon_t\rVert_{\psi_2}\le C_{\mathrm{hi}}\).
The absolute-regularity coefficients satisfy \(\beta(k)\le C_{\mathrm{hi}}\exp(-c_{\mathrm{lo}}k)\) for every \(k\ge0\).
For predictor \(k\), every original date in block \(\ell\) enters with the known coefficient \(S_{k\ell}/n_\ell\).
The map \(\xi\) is twice continuously differentiable and locally one-to-one on the finite-dimensional rank-\(r\) Gaussian signal-and-noise manifold \(\Theta_n^{\mathrm G}\) at \(\theta_0\).
On the local submodel, pre-period errors and donor-only post-period errors are independent and identically distributed Gaussian vectors with the covariance submatrices induced by \(\Sigma\).

definitions.name: Block-stable fixed-rank panel class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n=\{P_n:P_n\text{ obeys every member property listed in }\texttt{by-member-properties}\}\), with the triangular-array index \(n\), all dimensions, and all fixed constants governed by those displayed properties.

definitions.name: Global admissible signal-and-error parameter space
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_n=\{\theta=(A,a_0,d,\Sigma,\mathsf Q_{\varepsilon}):\operatorname{rank}(A)=r,\ c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le\sigma_r(A)\le\sigma_1(A)\le C_{\mathrm{hi}},\ \lambda_{\min}(\Sigma)\ge c_{\mathrm{lo}},\ \lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)\le C_{\mathrm{hi}},\text{ there exist bounded }(F_{\mathrm{pre}},U_D,\mu_0,f_{\mathrm{post}})\text{ satisfying }A=F_{\mathrm{pre}}U_D,\ a_0=F_{\mathrm{pre}}\mu_0,\ d^{\prime}=f_{\mathrm{post}}^{\prime}U_D,\text{ and }\theta\text{ satisfies every condition indexed in }\texttt{by-member-properties}\}\), at triangular-array index \(n\). The rank equality forces \(F_{\mathrm{pre}}\) and \(U_D\) to have rank \(r\), so \(a_0\in\operatorname{col}(A)\) and \(d\in\operatorname{row}(A)\) are consequences rather than separate restrictions. The error-law coordinate \(\mathsf Q_{\varepsilon}\) carries the stationary dependence, tail, mixing, and long-run covariance features; \(J,K,L,r,\{n_\ell\},T_1,S,\rho,c_{\mathrm{lo}},C_{\mathrm{hi}}\) are fixed design coordinates governed by the same listed properties.

definitions.name: Observed-panel law map
definitions.construction: For \(\theta\in\Theta_n\), define \(\mathsf P_n(\theta)=P_\theta\) as the pushforward of \(\mathsf Q_{\varepsilon}\) under \(Y_t=(a_{0\ell},A_{\ell\cdot})^{\prime}+\varepsilon_t\) for every pre-treatment \(t\) in block \(\ell\), and \(Y_{D,t}=d+\varepsilon_{D,t}\) for the \(T_1\) observed donor-only post-treatment dates, with the target post coordinate projected out. Equip \(\Theta_n\) with the product Borel sigma-field generated by Euclidean signal coordinates and finite-dimensional cylinder probabilities of \(\mathsf Q_{\varepsilon}\), and equip panel laws with the evaluation sigma-field.

definitions.name: Gaussian local parameter manifold
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_n^{\mathrm G}=\{\theta\in\Theta_n:\mathsf Q_{\varepsilon}\text{ is the law of independent }N(0,\Sigma)\text{ vectors over all pre dates and induces independent }N(0,\Sigma_{DD})\text{ donor vectors over all observed post dates}\}\), with the rank and spectral constraints inherited from \(\Theta_n\).

definitions.name: Same-panel block-moment vector and covariance estimate
definitions.construction: \(\widehat z\) stacks the \(L\) target-plus-donor block means, the donor-only post mean, and \(n^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\sum_{t\in\ell}(Y_t-\overline Y_\ell)(Y_t-\overline Y_\ell)^{\prime}\); \(\widehat V\) is the corresponding block/HAC covariance estimator formed from \(\widehat\phi_t\) with logarithmic bandwidth and explicit deletion of the finitely many block-boundary lag pairs.

definitions.name: Rank-respecting joint moment confidence region
definitions.construction: \(E_n=\{\theta\in\Theta_n:n(\widehat z-z(\theta))^{\prime}\widehat V^{-1}(\widehat z-z(\theta))\le\chi^2_{q_z,1-\alpha}\}\), using a fixed positive-definite regularization of \(\widehat V\) on its vanishing-probability failure event. Thus every element of \(E_n\) indexes an admissible observed-panel law through \(\theta\mapsto P_\theta\).

definitions.name: Shifted-critical-cone local risk map
definitions.construction: At the local center set \(c_{0,0}=d_0^{\prime}A_0^+a_{0,0}\) and \(b_0=c_{0,0}-d_0^{\prime}w_0\). Compute \(\dot c(u)\) by differentiating the completion along \(\theta_n(u)\) at \(\theta_0\), compute \(h(u,t)=\arg\min_{h\in\mathcal C_0}\{\tfrac12h^{\prime}H_0h+Q(u,t)^{\prime}h\}\), and set \(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)=a(u)+g^{\prime}h(u,t)\).

definitions.name: Honest Gaussian risk-curve bands
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_{1-\alpha}=\{C:C(Z,t)\text{ is a randomized measurable interval for every }t\in\mathcal D,\ \inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\Pr_u[\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)\in C(Z,t)\ \forall t\in\mathcal D]\ge1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: Compact-locally honest observed-panel band sequences
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{panel}}_{1-\alpha}(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)=\{\{\widetilde C_n\}_{n\ge1}:\widetilde C_n(v)\text{ is a randomized measurable interval based only on the observed Gaussian panel, and }\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\Pr_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}[R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))\in\widetilde C_n(v_n(t))\ \forall t\in\mathcal D]\ge1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: Certified finite acceptance-subset program
definitions.construction: For a coverage level \(q\in[0,1]\), the \(\delta\)-net \(\mathcal U_N\), cells \(o\in\mathcal O_h\), probabilities \(p_{io}\), and subset costs \(c_A\), define \(V_{N,h}(q)\) as the linear-program minimum of \(\zeta\) over \(x_{oA}\ge0\): \(\sum_Ax_{oA}=1\), \(\sum_op_{io}\sum_{A\ni i}x_{oA}\ge q\), and \(\sum_op_{io}\sum_Ac_Ax_{oA}\le\zeta\) for every \(i\). Its dual maximizes \(q\sum_i\ell_i+\sum_o\eta_o\) over \(\pi_i,\ell_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i\pi_i=1\), and unrestricted \(\eta_o\), subject to \(\eta_o\le c_A\sum_i\pi_ip_{io}-\sum_{i\in A}\ell_ip_{io}\) for every \((o,A)\).

definitions.name: Gaussian--Wishart deficiency-transfer handle
definitions.construction: Start from the exact Gaussian sufficient statistics consisting of the \(L\) independent block means, the donor-only post mean, and the pre and post residual scatter matrices; center them in the chart \(\xi\), separate parameter-free ancillary rotations, and construct parameter-independent randomization kernels whose uniform total-variation deficiencies vanish on \(\mathcal U\).

statements.statement: The map \(\mathsf P_n:\Theta_n\to\mathcal M_n\), \(\theta\mapsto P_\theta\), is measurable. Every \(\theta\in\Theta_n\) induces \(P_\theta\in\mathcal M_n\), every \(P\in\mathcal M_n\) has at least one representing \(\theta\in\Theta_n\), and all representing parameters agree on \(z(\theta)\), \(w_{P_\theta}\), and \(R_{P_\theta}\).
statements.justification: This lemma makes the global confidence region and its risk projection range over one coherent admissible parameterization of observed-panel laws.
statements.gap: The synthetic-control moment literature states law classes and identified coordinates separately; the risk-graph projection requires an explicit measurable bridge between them.
statements.consumer: The global band can be implemented over rank-respecting parameter coordinates without silently projecting over objects that fail to define observed-panel laws.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_n\), the target untreated post-regime mean is identified from observed-law means by \(c_0=d^{\prime}A^+a_0\); this value is invariant across all solutions of \(A\gamma=a_0\) and across factor rotations.
statements.justification: This lemma makes prediction risk an observed-law functional even though the treated target's post-treatment counterfactual is missing.
statements.gap: Fry2024MomentsSC derives moment-based synthetic-control limits; the displayed row-span completion for this block-stable risk target is the necessary identifying move rather than a corrected treatment-effect formula.
statements.consumer: A synthetic-control analyst can evaluate population counterfactual risk without using treated target outcomes after intervention.

statements.statement: The map \(v\mapsto w_P(v)\) admits a complete finite semialgebraic stratification indexed by \(B\) and strict-slack sign patterns. On support \(B\), the formulas \((w_B)_B=H_{BB}^{-1}(f_B-\eta_B\mathbf 1)\), \((w_B)_{B^c}=0\), and \(s_{B^c}=H_{B^cB}(w_B)_B-f_{B^c}+\eta_B\mathbf 1\) are valid exactly when \((w_B)_B>0\) and \(s_{B^c}\ge0\). Consequently, \(G_P\) is an observable semialgebraic graph.
statements.justification: The finite face atlas is the computational substrate for both the global graph and the local optimal-band problem.
statements.gap: CanenSong2026SimplexWeight and HsiehShiShum2022MathProgramming encode one fixed constrained optimizer; neither stratifies a continuum of predictor-indexed population objectives and its risk graph.
statements.consumer: Implementations can enumerate exactly which donor face supports each proposed predictor weighting before reporting risk uncertainty.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_n\), the estimator \(\widehat z\) has a joint root-\(n\) asymptotic linear expansion driven by weighted contiguous-block sums of \(\phi_t\), including the covariance between mean and second-moment estimation; the block/HAC estimator \(\widehat V\) is uniformly consistent for the resulting nonsingular covariance \(V(P)\).
statements.justification: Same-panel inference must propagate pre-weight estimation and covariance estimation jointly; fixed-weight post error variance is not the estimator variance.
statements.gap: Fry2024MomentsSC supplies fixed-donor mixing limits, while CattaneoFengTitiunik2021PredictionIntervals separates fitted-weight and future-outcome errors; the required joint block-mean and residual-covariance expansion for population MSE is not given there.
statements.consumer: The expansion supports feasible uncertainty quantification without sample splitting or target post-treatment counterfactuals.

statements.statement: The band \(C_n\) is measurable and satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_n}\Pr_P\{R_P(v)\in C_n(v)\text{ for every }v\in\Delta_K\}\ge1-\alpha\), together with the explicit uniform stochastic diameter bound \(\lim_{M_{\mathrm{wid}}\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_n}\Pr_P\{\sup_{v\in\Delta_K}\sqrt n\,\operatorname{diam}C_n(v)>M_{\mathrm{wid}}\}=0\). Hence every measurable same-panel selector \(\widehat v\in\Delta_K\) obeys \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_n}\Pr_P\{R_P(\widehat v)\in C_n(\widehat v)\}\ge1-\alpha\), including sequences within \(O(n^{-1/2})\) of any donor-face change.
statements.justification: This is the first same-panel certificate for the entire population prediction-risk graph and automatically protects unsplit predictor tuning.
statements.gap: VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection and PouliotXieLiu2026DegreesFreedom tune predictors without an honest full-risk-graph band; CanenSong2026SimplexWeight covers a fixed objective rather than a continuum whose donor face moves.
statements.consumer: An implementation of the displayed fixed-ridge quadratic simplex estimator can compare predictor weights and retain a valid risk certificate after selecting one on the same pre panel; the theorem does not certify the different objectives implemented by Synth or SparseSC.

statements.statement: Uniformly on \(\mathcal U\times\mathcal D\), \(w_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))=w_0+n^{-1/2}h(u,t)+O(n^{-1})\) and \(\sqrt n\{R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))-R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v_0)\}=\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)+o(1)\). The map \(\Psi_{\theta_0}\) is continuous piecewise affine on finitely many polyhedral critical-cone cells and retains mean-completion, donor-mean, covariance-risk, and donor-weight derivatives.
statements.justification: The shifted critical-cone expansion is the correct local graph when moment noise and predictor queries move active faces at the same root-\(n\) scale.
statements.gap: Geyer1994ConstrainedM and FangSantos2019Directional analyze a fixed constraint map; this result must keep the root-\(n\) movement of the query and the KKT slack jointly and uniformly over a compact direction set.
statements.consumer: The local curve is the input needed to calibrate face-aware simultaneous bands rather than a pointwise fixed-cone approximation.

statements.statement: For the family \(u\mapsto\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,\cdot)\), every admissible interval band can be replaced without larger loss or smaller coverage by the pointwise envelope of the parameter curves it accepts. Its maximum width equals the \(d_{\Psi}\)-diameter of that acceptance set. For each pair \((u,u')\), \(d_{\Psi}(u,u')\) is the maximum of finitely many second-order-cone programs obtained by intersecting the two critical-cone cell systems with \(\mathcal D\).
statements.justification: This reduction replaces an infinite-dimensional band action by a confidence-set decision under a computable geometry-specific diameter loss.
statements.gap: FreybergerRai2018UniformBands, Definition 1, restricts bands to those induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands. Its Section 2.3 leads with weighted area; Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, while the paper supplies low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation specifically for weighted area. The separate unresolved target here is the externally randomized max-curve-diameter decision problem over all measurable interval-section bands. EvansHansenStark2005MinimaxConfidence instead uses additive set measure rather than curve diameter.
statements.consumer: A numerical solver can compute exact pairwise curve distances with primal and dual conic certificates.

statements.statement: Let \(q=1-\alpha\). For every parameter mesh \(\delta\), observation mesh \(h\), and truncation radius \(R\), the primal and dual finite programs defining \(V_{N,h}\), with interval-certified Gaussian cell probabilities and conic curve distances, provide explicit computable lower and upper bounds on \(L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\). If \(\delta\to0\), \(R\to\infty\), \(hR\to0\), and numerical enclosure errors vanish, the certified gap converges to zero. The resulting envelope rules are asymptotically minimax in the Gaussian shift experiment over all externally randomized measurable interval-section bands; the comparison class is not restricted to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set.
statements.justification: The theorem determines the hard local decision value by converging certified finite programs rather than restating its defining infimum.
statements.gap: SchaferStark2009OptimalRegions approximates minimum expected measure using test inversion, and ArmstrongKolesar2018OptimalInference solves scalar convex Gaussian functionals; neither covers nonadditive maximum curve width for unrestricted randomized bands on a piecewise-affine KKT graph.
statements.consumer: Researchers receive auditable lower and upper certificates for the unavoidable simultaneous risk-band cost at a chosen predictor and panel configuration.

statements.statement: Can one construct parameter-independent Markov kernels between the exact Gaussian block-mean and residual-scatter experiment generated by the observed panel and \(Z\sim N(u,I(\theta_0)^{-1})\) whose deficiencies vanish uniformly for \(u\in\mathcal U\), while simultaneously transporting the bounded curve-diameter loss, repairing vanishing coverage deficits, and preserving \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U,t\in\mathcal D}|\sqrt n\{R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))-R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v_0)\}-\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)|\to0\)?
statements.justification: This is the genuine unresolved step: LAN weak convergence alone does not transfer simultaneous coverage and worst-case expected maximum width for arbitrary randomized bands.
statements.gap: LeCamYang2000 gives experiment-comparison tools, but no located result supplies this compact-local Gaussian--Wishart transfer for a moving-KKT curve target and a discontinuous coverage constraint.
statements.consumer: Closing the transfer makes the computed Gaussian benchmark a sharp statement about procedures using the actual partially observed panel.

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}>0\), there exists a sequence \(\{\widetilde C_n^{(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}})}\}\in\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{panel}}_{1-\alpha}(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\) such that \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\mathbb E_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}[\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\sqrt n\,\operatorname{diam}\widetilde C_n^{(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}})}(v_n(t))]\le L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\). Conversely, for every generic sequence \(\{\widetilde C_n\}\in\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{panel}}_{1-\alpha}(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\mathbb E_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}[\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\sqrt n\,\operatorname{diam}\widetilde C_n(v_n(t))]\ge L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\). There exists a diagonal sequence in this honesty class for which the limit equals \(L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)\), and its rules inherit the certified finite upper and lower decision bounds. These quantifiers do not refer to the global projection band \(C_n\), for which no global minimax claim is made.
statements.justification: This matching lower bound and attainment theorem is the field-level payoff: it quantifies the exact risk-certificate cost through moving donor constraints.
statements.gap: CanenSong2026SimplexWeight proves uniform validity for a fixed optimizer. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands, Definition 1, restricts attention to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out random selection among valid bands; Section 2.3 leads with weighted area, and its generic-objective Theorem 2 is accompanied by low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation specifically for weighted area. Independently of those results, the unresolved target is the unrestricted externally randomized local max-curve-diameter value and its sharp transfer to a synthetic-control panel.
statements.consumer: Software implementing the displayed fixed-ridge quadratic simplex estimator can report how much simultaneous risk uncertainty is information-theoretically unavoidable near the chosen donor-face geometry.

statements.statement: Under the single criterion \(L_\alpha\), if the critical cone \(\mathcal C_0\) is a linear space, then \(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)=a_{\star}^{\prime}u+b_{\star}^{\prime}t\) and the risk-graph decision reduces exactly to scalar Gaussian confidence-interval inference for \(a_{\star}^{\prime}u\). At a boundary face the same certified program applies, and the difference from a separated face may be positive, zero, or negative after the information and derivatives change; no compulsory positive kink penalty is asserted.
statements.justification: A common decision criterion gives an honest separated-face benchmark and rules out a spurious universal boundary surcharge.
statements.gap: Generic constrained-estimator theory distinguishes tangent cones but does not compare optimal simultaneous curve-band costs under the observed-panel information.
statements.consumer: Practitioners can tell whether a donor-face transition actually raises the certified cost in their local configuration rather than applying a blanket penalty.

statements.statement: Consider the one-dimensional iid Gaussian subexperiment with \(r=2,J=3,K=L=2\), \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \(T_1/n\to\lambda=1\), \(S=I_2\), and \(\rho=1/20\). Fix \(U_D=[(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)]\), \(\mu_0=(3/2,3/2)^{\prime}\), \(f_{\mathrm{post}}=(1,0)^{\prime}\), \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,4,1)\) in target--donor order, and independent Gaussian errors across every pre and post date. Let the scalar \(a>0\) multiply the first pre-factor row, so \(F_{\mathrm{pre}}(a)=\operatorname{diag}(a,1)\), and take the scalar chart \(\xi(\theta)=a-1\). The center \(a=1\) has \(F_{\mathrm{pre},0}=I_2\), \(A_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(a_{0,0}=(3/2,3/2)^{\prime}\), \(d_0=(0,1,0)^{\prime}\), \(c_{0,0}=d_0^{\prime}A_0^+a_{0,0}=3/2\), \(X_0=A_0\), and \(x_0=a_{0,0}\). The path \(a_n(u)=1+u/\sqrt n\) varies only this first pre-factor row; \(U_D,\mu_0,f_{\mathrm{post}},S,\rho,\Sigma,p,\lambda\), the Gaussian error law, and every other nuisance coordinate are fixed. Along this path \(d_n(u)^{\prime}A_n(u)^+a_{0,n}(u)=3/2\), so \(\dot c(u)=0\). Hence \(A_n(u)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1+u/\sqrt n&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(a_{0,n}(u)=(3(1+u/\sqrt n)/2,3/2)^{\prime}\), and \(d_n(u)=d_0\), so the post sample carries no information about \(u\). At the center, with \(v=(s,1-s)\), \(w_{P_{\theta_0}}(v)=(0,z,1-z)\), \(z=\operatorname{clip}((40s-9)/22,0,1)\), \(b_0=c_{0,0}-d_0^{\prime}w_0=1/2\) at \(s_0=31/40\), and \(R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v)=17/4-5z+6z^2\). Query \(v_n(t)=(s_0+t/\sqrt n,1-s_0-t/\sqrt n)\) for \(|t|\le L_0/\sqrt2\). The affected first-block mean derivative in target--donor order is \(D m_1=(3/2,0,1,0)^{\prime}\), while every other mean and covariance derivative is zero. Therefore the information per \(n\) observations is exactly \(I=p_1D m_1^{\prime}\Sigma^{-1}D m_1=\tfrac12\{9/4+1/4\}=5/4\). The upper KKT boundary has derivative \(-31/80\) in \(a\), while the unclipped second-donor weight has derivatives \(20/11\) in \(s\) and \(31/44\) in \(a\); since the centered risk derivative satisfies \(R_{P_{\theta_0}}^{\prime}(1)=7\), the local curve is \(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)=7\min\{(20/11)t+(31/44)u,0\}\). For \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and \(0<m=m_{\mathrm{half}}\le\min\{M,80L_0/(31\sqrt2)\}\), the query set contains a point at which both curves for \(u\in\{-m,m\}\) are unsaturated, and the exact binary minimax width is \((217m/22)\max\{\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-2m\sqrt{5/4})-\alpha,0\}\). The decision rule is on its unsaturated positive branch exactly when additionally \(m<z_{1-\alpha}/\sqrt{5/4}\); on that interval the maximum operator may be deleted.
statements.justification: The explicit hinge verifies that the local graph is nonconstant at a moving boundary and that zero extra simultaneous-graph cost remains possible.
statements.gap: No cited synthetic-control result solves this bounded Gaussian confidence decision; the calculation is a falsifiable sanity reduction, not the full multidimensional theorem.
statements.consumer: The smallest nontrivial implementation test has a closed-form benchmark against which the certified program can be checked.

sampling_model.design: One target and \(J\) fixed donors are observed for \(n\) pre-treatment dates partitioned into \(L\) known proportional blocks; only the \(J\) untreated donors enter the \(T_1\) stable post-regime sample used for risk estimation.
sampling_model.units: The cross section is fixed. Pre-block and post-regime means obey the rank-\(r\) factor representation; \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=r\) then implies \(a_0\in\operatorname{col}(A)\) and \(d\in\operatorname{row}(A)\).
sampling_model.treatment: The target may be treated in the post period, but its post outcomes are excluded from the observed-data experiment for \(R_P\).
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is needed; identification is the row-span completion induced by the stable common-loading model.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate block means and donor post means by averages, \(\Sigma\) by pre-block-demeaned residual second moments, and their joint long-run covariance by block/HAC scores. The local optimality theorem uses the exact information in Gaussian block means and pre/post scatter statistics.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 establish sparse predictor selection consistency and a faster predictor-match mean-squared-error rate, without inference for population prediction risk along the tuning path.
Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid joint inference for a simplex optimizer and its functional at one fixed population objective through polyhedral-cone projection.
Theorems 1--2 and Theorem A give probability-guaranteed prediction intervals for a future synthetic-control counterfactual after propagating estimated-weight and post-regime errors.

Definition 1 restricts bands to those induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands; Section 2.3 leads with weighted area; Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, with low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation supplied specifically for weighted area.
Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 give Bayes--minimax duality for confidence sets under expected additive measure, and Theorem 2 solves a bounded one-dimensional shift family.
Theorem 2 proves convergence of a Monte Carlo approximation to a finite-prior minimax expected-measure confidence procedure.
Theorem 3.1 and its corollaries derive finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for scalar linear functionals over convex Gaussian regression classes.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 characterize ordinary-bootstrap failure and validate derivative-aware resampling for a fixed directionally differentiable functional.
Propositions 3.1--3.6 provide active-set degrees of freedom and information criteria for selecting synthetic-control penalties or predictor-weighting matrices.

tldr: Predictor weighting changes both the donor face and the future counterfactual performance of a synthetic control, yet current methods either tune one weight vector or report inference for one fixed constrained optimizer. This proposal identifies the entire population prediction-MSE graph from a block-stable fixed-rank panel, constructs an honest root-\(n\) same-panel band over the full predictor simplex, and solves the compact-local Gaussian decision problem for minimum worst-case expected maximum width by finite KKT-cell, conic-distance, and primal--dual linear programs with certified vanishing error. The central open step is an experiment-level Gaussian--Wishart transfer strong enough to preserve simultaneous coverage and expected maximum width for unrestricted randomized bands.

project_justification.gap: VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection and PouliotXieLiu2026DegreesFreedom make predictor selection operational but do not attach an honest population-risk certificate to every candidate weighting. CanenSong2026SimplexWeight treats one fixed simplex objective. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands restricts attention to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and develops low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation for weighted area; other minimum-size confidence-set results treat scalar linear targets or additive set-measure losses. None addresses an unrestricted externally randomized max-curve-diameter decision for a piecewise-affine risk curve whose KKT face moves with the local query.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the observable graph \(G_P\) together with the exact compact-local price, measured by worst-case expected maximum interval width, of covering that graph when predictor and moment perturbations move donor faces on the same root-\(n\) scale.
project_justification.fill: The project combines row-span completion, a joint block-mean and covariance expansion, exact shifted-QP inversion, critical-cone curve geometry, certified finite primal and dual decision programs, and a matching local asymptotic lower-bound and attainment transfer from the actual observed Gaussian panel.

related_work: VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection is the writing exemplar: its Introduction frames predictor weights as determinants of performance and interpretability, and Theorems 1--2 settle sparse support recovery and predictor-match rates rather than risk inference. CanenSong2026SimplexWeight, Section 2.5 and Theorem 3.1, is the closest constrained-inference method exemplar; its adaptive cone projection is used as the fixed-objective benchmark, while the present target couples a continuum of objectives and locally shifting slack. CattaneoFengTitiunik2021PredictionIntervals, Lemmas 1--2 and Theorems 1--2, supplies the uncertainty-decomposition discipline, but its target is a future counterfactual outcome rather than unconditional population MSE. FangSantos2019Directional, Theorems 3.1--3.2, explains why an ordinary bootstrap at a fixed nonsmooth map is unreliable; the local map here additionally changes with the predictor query. EvansHansenStark2005MinimaxConfidence, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, and SchaferStark2009OptimalRegions, Sections 2--4, provide the Bayes--minimax and finite-program architecture for additive expected size. ArmstrongKolesar2018OptimalInference, Theorem 3.1, is the decision-theoretic writing exemplar for turning honesty into a computable efficiency benchmark, but its functional is scalar and linear. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands, Definition 1, restricts its band class to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands. Its Section 2.3 leads with weighted area. Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, but the paper supplies low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation specifically for weighted area. The present departure is stated independently: externally randomized measurable band actions, simultaneous maximum KKT-curve-diameter loss, and an observed-panel local minimax transfer. No strict numerical separation from Freyberger--Rai is asserted. PouliotXieLiu2026DegreesFreedom, Propositions 3.1--3.6, gives active-set information criteria for tuning; it informs the motivation for same-panel selection but does not implement the fixed-ridge objective studied here. The proposed certificate is for the displayed fixed-ridge quadratic simplex estimator and does not directly certify the different objectives implemented by Synth or SparseSC. Exact-pair searches through September 2026 found no published all-predictor population-MSE band or unrestricted randomized minimax-width solution for a moving-KKT synthetic-control risk graph. The March 2026 Martinez--Vives-i-Bastida preliminary work is adjacent research on synthetic-control predictor choice, but it is non-archival and is not used as a theorem-level comparator; the present target is the full population-risk graph and its unrestricted expected-maximum-width decision value.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve derivations of the KKT atlas, the critical-cone risk map, and the finite acceptance-subset primal and dual have checkable algebra and an exactly solved binary hinge benchmark, but they are not treated as established. The proof must still close the uniform mixing CLT and HAC step, multiple-weak-face uniform remainder, measurable-band regularization, interval-certified computation, and especially the compact-local Gaussian--Wishart experiment transfer. Floating-point agreement at the hinge is diagnostic only. The global projection band is a validity construction only and is not asserted to be globally minimax; local optimality quantifies over the separate generic class \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{panel}}_{1-\alpha}\).
honest_scope: The global mixing-class band and the locally optimal Gaussian-neighborhood bands may be different procedures. Rank, donor count, predictor count, and block count are fixed; the rank is known and spectrally separated; the ridge is fixed positive; block means and the post regime are stable. The target is the displayed fixed-ridge quadratic simplex estimator, which is distinct from the objectives currently implemented by Synth and SparseSC; direct guarantees for those packages are not claimed. Unknown rank, growing dimensions, arbitrary singleton-date predictors, post-factor drift, shrinking ridge, and optimal inference for a corrected causal treatment effect are excluded. The linear-critical-cone reduction recovers ordinary scalar Gaussian interval inference on separated faces, and the explicit hinge shows that a moving boundary need not impose a positive extra width cost. The global parameter region is indexed by \(\Theta_n\) and the measurable observed-law map \(\theta\mapsto P_\theta\). Global minimaxity of \(C_n\) is not claimed; the local minimax comparison ranges over generic compact-locally honest sequences \(\widetilde C_n\). The March 2026 Martinez--Vives-i-Bastida preliminary work is treated only as adjacent non-archival research, not as an established theorem comparator.

novelty_justification: The closest constrained-inference result is CanenSong2026SimplexWeight, Theorem 3.1, which covers a weight and functional at one fixed population objective. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands, Definition 1, restricts attention to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands; Section 2.3 leads with weighted area, and although Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, the paper provides low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation specifically for weighted area. The present departure is independent and narrower than any claim of numerical dominance: it asks for minimax worst-case expected maximum KKT-curve diameter over unrestricted externally randomized measurable interval-section rules and for transfer of that value to the observed panel. EvansHansenStark2005MinimaxConfidence and SchaferStark2009OptimalRegions optimize additive expected set measure, for which marginal inclusion probabilities suffice, whereas the present loss is the nonadditive maximum width of a curve envelope. The first changed proof step is therefore not a routine directional delta method: it is the reduction to whole acceptance-subset decisions under the KKT-curve pseudometric, followed by certified finite primal and dual programs and a compact-local Gaussian--Wishart transfer for unrestricted bands. The synthetic-control component is also not a relabeling of a treatment-effect interval. The estimand is unconditional counterfactual prediction MSE for the displayed fixed-ridge objective, whose derivative necessarily retains row-span completion, covariance estimation, and population-weight movement. Exact-pair searches through September 2026 found no paper subsuming this combined kernel.
